title: Sight Words Made Simple: No-Tears Method
meta: Teach sight words for kindergarten reading with the Dolch list using this no-tears method. Practical steps parents can use daily to build strong reading skills at home.
h1: Sight Words Made Simple: A No-Tears Method for Kindergarten Reading

sections.h2: What Sight Words Are and Why They Matter
sections.body: Sight words are common words kids see in books that do not follow regular phonics rules. Mastering them helps kindergarten reading flow faster. Focus first on the Dolch list which has 40 words for pre-kindergarten and 52 for kindergarten.

sections.h2: Using the Dolch List for Steady Progress
sections.body: Start with the Dolch list pre-primer words like the, and, a, to, I. Print one list per week. Have your child read each word three times then use it in a short sentence. This builds kindergarten reading without pressure.

Keep sessions to five minutes. Point to the word, say it together, then trace it on paper. If your child hesitates, move to the next word and return later. Celebrate every correct read with a high-five to keep it encouraging.

Write Dolch list words on index cards and sort them into piles of known and new. Use sidewalk chalk outside to write and read them. Pair this with our reading tools and audiobooks on Gumroad for extra practice without screens.

Keep a simple chart showing words mastered each week. When your child hits ten new words from the Dolch list, reward with a coloring book from our Gumroad store. This steady system turns sight words practice into a habit that lasts.

faq.q: How many sight words should a kindergartener learn?
faq.a: Aim for 20 to 30 Dolch list words by the end of kindergarten through short daily practice.

faq.q: What if my child gets frustrated with sight words?
faq.a: Shorten the session to three minutes and use only three words from the Dolch list until they feel confident.
